rubric.why: Density is defined as mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining density as mass per unit volume.

rubric.why: Elasticity is the property that enables a body to return to its original form after the deforming force is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a body regains its original shape or size when the deforming force is removed.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
Elasticity is the property of a body by which it regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.

items.followUp: Derive the second equation of motion using a velocity-time graph.

rubric.why: The derivation uses initial velocity u, final velocity v, and time t on the velocity-time graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying u, v and t on the velocity-time graph.

rubric.why: The slope of a velocity-time graph represents acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using the graph's slope as acceleration.

rubric.why: This is the acceleration relation obtained from the graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly deriving a = (v - u)/t or its rearrangement.

rubric.why: This is the first equation of motion.
rubric.description: States the first equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining v = u + at.

modelAnswer: Draw a velocity-time graph with time t on the horizontal axis and velocity on the vertical axis.
Let the velocity increase uniformly from u at t = 0 to v at time t.
The slope of the graph is acceleration, a = (v - u)/t.
Therefore, at = v - u.
Hence, v = u + at, the first equation of motion.

items.followUp: State and explain the two conditions for rotational equilibrium.

rubric.why: Zero resultant force is the first condition for equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant force is zero.

rubric.why: When the resultant force is zero, there is no linear acceleration; the body remains at rest or moves with uniform velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the body has no linear acceleration, or remains at rest or in uniform motion.

rubric.why: Zero resultant torque is the second condition for equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant torque is zero.

rubric.why: When the resultant torque is zero, there is no angular acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the body has no angular acceleration.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when it has no linear or angular acceleration.
First condition: the resultant force acting on the body must be zero, ΣF = 0.
Therefore, the body has no linear acceleration and remains at rest or moves with uniform velocity.
Second condition: the resultant torque acting on the body must be zero, Στ = 0.
Therefore, the body has no angular acceleration.

items.followUp: An object weighs 25 N in air and 15 N in water. Calculate its density and suggest a possible material.

rubric.why: The loss of weight in water is 18 N − 11.4 N = 6.6 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for calculating the loss of weight as 6.6 N.

rubric.why: Relative density equals weight in air divided by loss of weight in water: 18/6.6 ≈ 2.73.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining a relative density of approximately 2.73 using the correct ratio.

rubric.why: The object's density is approximately 2727 kg/m³, or 2.727 g/cm³.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct numerical density, approximately 2727 kg/m³ or 2.727 g/cm³.

rubric.why: A density answer must include an appropriate density unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an appropriate unit, such as kg/m³ or g/cm³.

rubric.why: A density close to 2.7 g/cm³ is characteristic of aluminium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying aluminium (aluminum) as a likely material.

modelAnswer: Given: weight in air = 18 N; weight in water = 11.4 N; density of water = 1000 kg/m^3.
Loss of weight in water = 18 N - 11.4 N = 6.6 N.
Formula: relative density = weight in air / loss of weight in water.
Relative density = 18 N / 6.6 N = 2.73.
Formula: density of object = relative density × density of water.
This density is close to that of aluminium, so the object may be made of aluminium.

items.followUp: What is meant by a derived quantity? Give two examples.

rubric.why: A physical quantity is a measurable property that can be expressed by a magnitude and a unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that physical quantities are measurable and expressed by magnitude and unit.

rubric.why: The question asks for two examples of physical quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving any two valid examples of physical quantities.

modelAnswer: Physical quantities are measurable properties of a body or phenomenon that can be expressed by a magnitude and a unit.
Examples include length and mass.
